mainTopic: יוצא דופן and the animal born after it: the מחלוקת of רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא over whether a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור, and how אביי and רבינא explain the ברייתא that defines בכור.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion, a צריכא explaining why two cases were both needed. Then a new משנה brings a case: an animal born by caesarean section (יוצא דופן) and the animal born naturally after it. רבי טרפון is unsure whether either one is a בכור, so both graze until they get a מום, and then the owner eats them. רבי עקיבא says neither is a בכור: the first did not open the womb (פטר רחם), and the second was not born first. The גמרא explains the root of their argument: does an animal that is a בכור in only one way (בכור לדבר אחד) count as a בכור? A ברייתא then defines בכור from the פסוקים, step by step: 'כל בכור' is narrowed by 'זכר', then 'פטר רחם', then 'בכור'. רב שרביא points out that the two halves of the ברייתא seem to contradict each other on בכור לדבר אחד. אביי answers that such an animal is not a בכור and rereads the first half. רבינא answers that it is a בכור and explains that the second half learns from 'בכור' being an extra word.

steps.title: Closing line: both cases were necessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier discussion. Both cases had to be taught, because otherwise one might think the offspring of the animal that had not given birth before is 'superior.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [One might have thought] that this one, which had not given birth before, is superior. Therefore it was necessary [to teach both cases].
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a discussion from the previous part of the דף. The גמרא concludes that teaching both cases was necessary (צריכא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked why two similar cases both had to be stated. Here it answers: without the second case, we might think the animal that had never given birth before has a stronger claim (it is 'שביח טפי'). So both cases are needed to block that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: the conclusion that each case had to be taught separately
Is more superior / has a stronger standing
Gave birth for the first time

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the סוגיא BEFORE the new משנה. Do not try to connect it to יוצא דופן. It is just the closing of the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: that this one, which had not [previously] given birth
phrases.notes: Refers to the case from the previous discussion

phrases.english: is more superior; [therefore] it was necessary.
phrases.notes: צריכא = the standard conclusion that both cases were needed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the צריכא discussion from the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases in the earlier משנה were necessary, because one might think the offspring of the animal that had not given birth before is superior.

steps.title: משנה: caesarean birth and the next animal — רבי טרפון's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a יוצא דופן followed by a naturally born animal. רבי טרפון says both must graze until they get a מום, and then the owner may eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An animal born by caesarean section, and the animal that is born after it. רבי טרפון says: both of them must graze until they become blemished, and they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a tricky case. The first animal came out by caesarean section, and the second came out naturally after it. רבי טרפון gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal has only half of what makes a בכור. The first was born first but did not open the womb. The second opened the womb but was not born first. רבי טרפון treats each as a ספק בכור. It cannot be given to the כהן, because the כהן cannot prove it is a בכור. It also cannot be used as ordinary חולין, because it might be holy. So it grazes until it gets a מום, and then the owner eats it.

keyTerms.meaning: Born through the side wall: a caesarean birth
They must graze until they become unfit (by getting a blemish)
In their blemished state
For the owners (not for the כהן)

steps.whyThisMatters: 'Graze until blemished, then the owner eats' is the standard ruling for a ספק בכור. It protects the possible קדושה, and it does not force the owner to give the animal away without proof.

phrases.english: MISHNA: An animal born by caesarean section
and the one that comes after it,
Rabbi Tarfon says:
both of them graze until they become blemished,
and they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.
phrases.notes: Not given to the כהן, because of the doubt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, both the יוצא דופן and the animal after it are a ספק בכור. They graze until blemished and are then eaten by the owner.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: neither animal is a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules that neither animal is a בכור. The first did not open the womb, and the second was not born first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: neither of them is a בכור. The first, because it is not 'פטר רחם' (the one that opens the womb). The second, because another one came before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי טרפון. He says clearly that neither animal is a בכור, and he gives a separate reason for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, a בכור must have both features: it must be first born AND it must open the womb. The first animal fails 'opening the womb.' The second animal fails 'being first.' Since neither has both, neither is a בכור, and both are fully ordinary animals.

keyTerms.meaning: That which opens the womb: the Torah's description of a בכור
That another preceded it

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור needs two things: being first AND opening the womb. In this case, each animal has only one of the two.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
neither of them is a firstborn,
the first, because it is not 'that which opens the womb,'
phrases.notes: It came out through the side, not through the womb opening

phrases.english: and the second, because another preceded it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר שְׁנֵיהֶן אֵינָן בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, neither animal is a בכור. The first is not פטר רחם, and the second was preceded by another.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא actually argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what deeper idea is behind the מחלוקת in the משנה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings look different, but the גמרא wants the one principle that splits them. Finding that principle will explain both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root principle)

phrases.english: GEMARA: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רבי טרפון from רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Is a 'firstborn in one respect' a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון is unsure whether an animal that is a בכור in only one way counts as a בכור. רבי עקיבא is sure that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון is in doubt about an animal that is a בכור in one respect: is it a בכור or is it not a בכור? And רבי עקיבא holds it is obvious that a בכור in one respect is not a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The argument is about a 'בכור לדבר אחד,' an animal that has only one of the two features of a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals in the משנה are 'firstborn in one respect.' רבי טרפון has a ספק, which is why he gives the doubtful ruling (graze until blemished). רבי עקיבא has no doubt: one feature is not enough, so both animals are ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt about it
A firstborn in only one respect (only first-born, or only first to open the womb)
It is obvious to him

steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת comes down to one question: does 'בכור לדבר אחד' count? רבי טרפון says ספק. רבי עקיבא says definitely not.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי טרפון does NOT say the animals are definitely בכורות. He is unsure. That is why the animals are not given to the כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon is uncertain:
[about] a firstborn in one respect,
whether it is a firstborn
or whether it is not a firstborn,
and to Rabbi Akiva it is obvious:
a firstborn in one respect
is not a firstborn.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור. רבי טרפון is in doubt, and רבי עקיבא holds that it clearly is not.

steps.title: ברייתא introduces a method for defining a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא introduces the דרשה method 'כלל הצריך לפרט ופרט הצריך לכלל' and asks how it works for the laws of בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: from a generalization that needs a detail, and from a detail that needs a generalization. How so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that will define a בכור from the פסוקים. This line only names the method and asks 'how?' It is setting up the derivation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this method, a general statement (כלל) and a specific detail (פרט) each need the other to be understood correctly. Neither one alone gives the full meaning. The ברייתא will now show this using the פסוקים about בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
A generalization that needs a detail to explain it
A detail that needs a generalization to explain it
How so? (introduces the example)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
from a generalization that requires a detail
and from a detail that requires a generalization,
how so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that defines בכור from the פסוקים, which connects to the question of what counts as a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The definition of בכור is derived through the method of כלל הצריך לפרט ופרט הצריך לכלל.

steps.title: 'All firstborn' is narrowed to males
steps.stepSummary: The general פסוק 'קדש לי כל בכור' might include females, so the Torah adds the detail 'זכר' to limit it to males.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn': one might think even a female is included. So the Torah says 'male.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins its derivation. The general פסוק (כלל) might include female animals, and a second פסוק (פרט) limits בכור to males. The derivation continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל בכור' sounds like it includes any firstborn, even a female. The פסוק in דברים that says 'כל הבכור… הזכר' is the פרט that narrows the כלל to males only. This is the first stage. Next, the ברייתא will show that the פרט itself also needs the כלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctify to Me every firstborn (שמות יג:ב), the כלל
One might have thought
Included in the meaning
Therefore the verse teaches

phrases.english: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn,'
one might think even a female is included?
Therefore the verse says 'male.'

steps.triggerLanguage: קַדֶּשׁ לִי כׇל בְּכוֹר יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ נְקֵבָה בַּמַּשְׁמָע
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כלל 'כל בכור' is limited by the פרט 'זכר': only males are בכור.

steps.title: Why the Torah adds 'opens the womb' after 'male'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. 'זכר' alone might include a male born after a female, so the Torah adds 'פטר רחם' to exclude that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had said only 'male,' you might think a male is a בכור even when a female was born before it. So the Torah says 'opens the womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with its chain of words. It now shows why the word 'זכר' is not enough on its own, and why the Torah also needed 'פטר רחם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used 'זכר' to limit בכור to males. But 'male' alone could include a male that came out after a female sister. 'פטר רחם' (opening the womb) tells us the animal itself must be the first to open the womb, and here the female already did that.

keyTerms.meaning: Opening the womb; the first to come out of the mother
A female
The verse comes to teach; introduces the extra word that settles the doubt
One might have thought

phrases.english: If only 'male' were written,
one might think it applies even if a female came out before it?
So the verse says: 'that which opens the womb.'
phrases.notes: The female opened the womb first, so the male that follows is not a פטר רחם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״זָכָר״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצְתָה נְקֵבָה לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's chain: after 'זכר' limits to males, 'פטר רחם' limits further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A male born after a female is not a בכור, learned from 'פטר רחם'.

steps.title: Why the Torah adds 'firstborn' after 'opens the womb'
steps.stepSummary: 'פטר רחם' alone might include an animal born naturally after an older sibling born by C-section, so the Torah adds 'בכור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had said only 'opens the womb,' you might think an animal is a בכור even if it came out after an older sibling born by C-section. So the Torah says 'firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its chain. It shows why 'פטר רחם' is not enough on its own, so the Torah also needed the word 'בכור'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born naturally after a C-section sibling really does open the womb, since nothing came out that way before it. But it is not the first child. The word 'בכור' (first one born) excludes it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born through the side wall of the mother (a C-section)
Firstborn; the first child born

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different animals. The יוצא דופן itself is the C-section animal. The animal in this case is a different one: the younger sibling, born naturally after it.

phrases.english: If only 'opens the womb' were written,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצָא אַחַר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן?
phrases.english: one might think it applies even if it came out after a sibling born by C-section?
So the verse says: 'firstborn.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצָא אַחַר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's chain with the last word, 'בכור'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal born naturally after a C-section sibling is not a בכור, learned from 'בכור'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same second animal that רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argued about (Steps 2–5): an animal that is a בכור in only one way. Here the ברייתא rules it is not a בכור.

steps.title: The two halves of the ברייתא seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא asks אביי: the רישא does not use 'בכור', which suggests a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור. The סיפא does use 'בכור', which suggests it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said to אביי: In the first part, the ברייתא does not use the word 'firstborn,' so it seems that an animal that is a firstborn in one way counts as a firstborn. In the last part, it does use the word 'firstborn,' so it seems that such an animal does not count as a firstborn!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא challenges the ברייתא. He says its two halves seem to hold opposite views on a בכור לדבר אחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male born after a female is first among the males, so it is a בכור in one way. If the word 'בכור' excluded anything that is not first in every way, the רישא could simply have used 'בכור'. Since it reached for 'פטר רחם' instead, it seems to think 'בכור' would not exclude it. Yet the סיפא uses 'בכור' to exclude a similar half-first animal.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that is a firstborn in only one way
The first part of the source
The last part of the source
Takes it up; cites it as the source
This shows that; apparently

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said to Abaye:
In the first clause, the teaching does not cite 'firstborn,'

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר.
phrases.english: which shows that a firstborn in one way is a firstborn.
In the last clause, the teaching does cite 'firstborn,'

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר!
phrases.english: which shows that a firstborn in one way is not a firstborn!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא לְאַבָּיֵי: רֵישָׁא לָא קָנָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא ״בְּכוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted and finds an internal contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא in Steps 8–9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving out 'בכור' in the רישא implies it counts as a בכור. Using 'בכור' in the סיפא implies it does not. The two halves cannot both be right.

steps.title: אביי: the first part is really about the C-section animal itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that a בכור לדבר אחד is not a בכור. He rereads the רישא as excluding the יוצא דופן itself, which only 'פטר רחם' can exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי answered: Really, a firstborn in one way is not a firstborn. The first part means this: If only 'male' were written, one might think even a C-section animal is a בכור. So the verse says 'opens the womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He keeps the סיפא as it is and explains the רישא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The C-section animal really was born first, so the word 'בכור' cannot exclude it. Only 'פטר רחם' can. That is why the רישא needed 'פטר רחם'. The female-first case is then excluded along with it, so the contradiction disappears and the סיפא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (used to keep the original position)
This is what it means; rereading a text

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: Actually, a firstborn in one way is not a firstborn,
and this is what the first clause means:

phrases.aramaic: אִי זָכָר, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן?
phrases.english: If only 'male' were written, one might think even a C-section animal is included?
So the verse says 'that which opens the womb.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, וְרֵישָׁא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שרביא's contradiction by rereading the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting one clause of the source (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא uses 'פטר רחם' for the female-first case, so 'בכור' would not have excluded it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא uses 'פטר רחם' for the C-section animal itself, which 'בכור' cannot exclude. A בכור לדבר אחד is not a בכור.

steps.title: רבינא: the word 'firstborn' excludes only because it would otherwise be extra
steps.stepSummary: רבינא holds that a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור. He rereads the סיפא: 'בכור' excludes the case only because it would otherwise be an extra word.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, a firstborn in one way is a firstborn. The last part means this: If you think an animal born after a C-section sibling is holy, why did the Torah need to write 'firstborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer to the contradiction. He keeps the רישא as it is and explains the סיפא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבינא, the plain meaning of 'בכור' would still include a half-first animal. But if this animal were holy, the word 'בכור' would add nothing. Since the Torah does not write extra words, 'בכור' must be there to exclude this case. The rule comes from the extra word, not from what the word means.

keyTerms.meaning: If it entered your mind; if you were to think
The Merciful One; the Torah
Why do I need it? (points to an extra word)
Holy; has the sanctity of a בכור

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a בכור לדבר אחד is not a בכור, and the רישא is about the C-section animal itself. רבינא: a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור, and the סיפא learns its rule from 'בכור' being an extra word.

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: Actually, a firstborn in one way is a firstborn,
and this is what the last clause means:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ יָצָא אַחֵר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן קָדוֹשׁ,
phrases.english: If you think that one which came out after a C-section sibling is holy,
why do I need the word 'firstborn' that the Torah wrote?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, וְסֵיפָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to רב שרביא's contradiction, taking the opposite position from אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the other clause; the rule comes from an extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא uses the meaning of 'בכור' to exclude a half-first animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור. The סיפא excludes its case only because 'בכור' would otherwise be extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי and רבינא take opposite sides of the question from Steps 4–5: does an animal that is a בכור in only one way count as a בכור? אביי's reading matches רבי עקיבא's certainty that it does not. רבינא's reading says it does count. רבי טרפון never held that view definitely; he only treated it as a ספק.
